sanskrit: pra su jyeṣṭhaṁ nicirābhyām bṛhan namo havyam matim bharatā mṛḻayadbhyāṁ svādiṣṭham mṛḻayadbhyām | tā samrājā ghṛtāsutī yajñe-yajña upastutā | athainoḥ kṣatraṁ na kutaś canādhṛṣe devatvaṁ nū cid ādhṛṣe ||
english: Bring forward the greatest offering, the rich oblation, the thought, to those twain who bestow grace most sweetly, most graciously. Those two sovereigns, consecrated with ghee, are praised at every sacrifice. Therefore their dominion cannot be assailed from anywhere, nor can their divinity ever be challenged.

sanskrit: adarśi gātur urave varīyasī panthā ṛtasya sam ayaṁsta raśmibhiś cakṣur bhagasya raśmibhiḥ | dyukṣam mitrasya sādanam aryamṇo varuṇasya ca | athā dadhāte bṛhad ukthyaṁ vaya upastutaṁ bṛhad vayaḥ ||
english: The broad, most spacious path of ṛta has been seen; it was gathered together by the rays of the sun, by the rays of Bhaga's eye. Luminous is the seat of Mitra, of Aryaman, and of Varuṇa. Thus they assume a great and laudable glory, a great glory sung in praise.

sanskrit: jyotiṣmatīm aditiṁ dhārayatkṣitiṁ svarvatīm ā sacete dive-dive jāgṛvāṁsā dive-dive | jyotiṣmat kṣatram āśāte ādityā dāvunas patī | mitras tayor varuṇo yātayajjano 'ryamā yātayajjanaḥ ||
english: They two, ever wakeful, ever watchful day by day, attend upon Aditi who bears light and sustains all living beings and the sunlit realm. Those Ādityas, lords of bounty, share the lustrous dominion. Mitra among them and Varuṇa order all men to righteousness, as does Aryaman who sets men aright.

sanskrit: ayam mitrāya varuṇāya śaṁtamaḥ somo bhūtv avapāneṣv ābhago devo deveṣv ābhagaḥ | taṁ devāso juṣerata viśve adya sajoṣasaḥ | tathā rājānā karatho yad īmaha ṛtāvānā yad īmahe ||
english: May this Soma, most health-bestowing, be the share of Mitra and Varuṇa at the draughts, the divine one sharing among the gods. May all the gods together delight in him today with one accord. So shall ye two kings who uphold ṛta grant what we implore of you, upholders of truth what we implore.

sanskrit: yo mitrāya varuṇāyāvidhaj jano 'narvāṇaṁ tam pari pāto aṁhaso dāśvāṁsam martam aṁhasaḥ | tam aryamābhi rakṣaty ṛjūyantam anu vratam | ukthair ya enoḥ paribhūṣati vrataṁ stomair ābhūṣati vratam ||
english: The mortal who has devoted worship to Mitra and Varuṇa without stumbling — him do ye protect, the bountiful man, from anguish, from sin. Aryaman guards him who walks upright in their ordinance. He who adorns their commandment with hymns, who decks their ordinance with songs of praise — him Aryaman protects.

sanskrit: namo dive bṛhate rodasībhyām mitrāya vocaṁ varuṇāya mīḻhuṣe sumṛḻīkāya mīḻhuṣe | indram agnim upa stuhi dyukṣam aryamaṇam bhagam | jyog jīvantaḥ prajayā sacemahi somasyo̍tī sacemahi ||
english: I would offer homage to great Heaven and to the two worlds; I would speak to Mitra and to bountiful Varuṇa, the most graciously merciful, most bountiful. Praise too the sky-dwelling Indra, Agni, Aryaman, and Bhaga. May we live long, accompanied by offspring, and be united under Soma's protection.

sanskrit: ūtī devānāṁ vayam indravanto maṁsīmahi svayaśaso marudbhiḥ | agnir mitro varuṇaḥ śarma yamsan tad aśyāma maghavāno vayaṁ ca ||
english: Under the protection of the gods, we with Indra as our ally and with the self-glorious Maruts, may we be favored. May Agni, Mitra, and Varuṇa grant us shelter — may we, the bountiful patrons, attain that boon, and we ourselves attain it.

sanskrit: suṣumā yātam adribhir gośrītā matsarā ime somāso matsarā ime | ā rājānā divispṛśāsmatrā gantam upa naḥ | ime vām mitrāvaruṇā gavāśiraḥ somāḥ śukrā gavāśiraḥ ||
english: Come hither readily, O Mitra and Varuṇa — these exhilarating Soma-draughts, pressed by the stones, mixed with milk, are ready, exhilarating. O ye two kings who touch the sky, come to us here. These Somas for you, O Mitra and Varuṇa, are blended with milk, bright, blended with milk.

sanskrit: ima ā yātam indavaḥ somāso dadhyāśiraḥ sutāso dadhyāśiraḥ | uta vām uṣaso budhi sākaṁ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ | suto mitrāya varuṇāya pītaye cārur ṛtāya pītaye ||
english: Come here to these drops, these Soma-juices blended with curds, pressed out and blended with curds. And at the dawning of the day, together with the rays of the sun, may the pressed Soma be offered to Mitra and Varuṇa to drink, the dear draught offered for drinking to ṛta.

sanskrit: tāṁ vāṁ dhenum na vāsarīm aṁśuṁ duhanty adribhiḥ somaṁ duhanty adribhiḥ | asmatrā gantam upa no 'rvāñcā somapītaye | ayaṁ vām mitrāvaruṇā nṛbhiḥ sutaḥ soma ā pītaye sutaḥ ||
english: Like a milch-cow at dawn they milk the Soma-stalk with the pressing-stones, they milk the Soma with the stones. Come hither to us, both of you, turn toward us for the drinking of Soma. This Soma, O Mitra and Varuṇa, has been pressed by men for you to drink, pressed for your drinking.

sanskrit: pra-pra pūṣṇas tuvijātasya śasyate mahitvam asya tavaso na tandate stotram asya na tandate | arcāmi sumnayann aham antyūtim mayobhuvam | viśvasya yo mana āyuyuve makho deva āyuyuve makhaḥ ||
english: Ever and again the greatness of Pūṣan, mightily born, is proclaimed; the praise of this vigorous one ceases not, his hymn of praise does not cease. I worship him, seeking his favor, him whose protection comes at the last and who brings well-being — Pūṣan the god who knits together the mind of all creation, who as the divine Makha knits all together.

sanskrit: pra hi tvā pūṣann ajiraṁ na yāmani stomebhiḥ kṛṇva ṛṇavo yathā mṛdha uṣṭro na pīparo mṛdhaḥ | huve yat tvā mayobhuvaṁ devaṁ sakhyāya martyaḥ | asmākam āṅgūṣān dyumninas kṛdhi vājeṣu dyumninas kṛdhi ||
english: I urge you forward, O Pūṣan, swift as a swift horse on the journey, with hymns as with a camel that overflows with milk — for you overcome resistance. I invoke you, the divine bringer of well-being, as a mortal calls for friendship. Make our praises full of splendor; make us glorious in contests.

sanskrit: yasya te pūṣan sakhye vipanyavaḥ kratvā cit santo 'vasā bubhujrira iti kratvā bubhujrire | tām anu tvā navīyasīṁ niyutaṁ rāya īmahe | aheḻamāna uruśaṁsa sarī bhava vāje-vāje sarī bhava ||
english: Those inspired sages who, even in their wisdom, have enjoyed your friendship and your protection, O Pūṣan, have indeed enjoyed it by their intelligence. Following that same path, we seek of you a fresher wealth, a band of treasure. O widely praised one, be not displeased — be our guide, be our guide at every contest.

sanskrit: asyā ū ṣu ṇa upa sātaye bhuvo 'heḻamāno rarivām̐ ajāśva śrasyatām ajāśva | o ṣu tvā vavṛtīmahi stomebhir dasma sādhubhiḥ | nahi tvā pūṣann atimanya āghṛṇe na te sakhyam pahanuve ||
english: O goat-horsed one, be present for us here, without displeasure, bringing gifts, for the winning of this booty — let the goat-drawn car speed on! We would turn you back toward us, O wonderful one, with these effective praises. Never, O Pūṣan, O radiant one, do I disregard you; never do I deny your friendship.

sanskrit: astu śrauṣaṭ puro agniṁ dhiyā dadha ā nu tac chardho divyaṁ vṛṇīmaha indravāyū vṛṇīmahe | yad dha krāṇā vivasvati nābhā saṁdāyi navyasī | adha pra sū na upa yantu dhītayo devāṁś acchā na dhītayaḥ ||
english: Let it be heard — śrauṣaṭ! First set Agni in place with devotion; now let us choose that divine host, let us choose Indra and Vāyu. When in the active one, at the navel of Vivasvat, the newer bond was made — then may our prayers come forth and go toward the gods, our prayers go toward them.

sanskrit: yad dha tyan mitrāvaruṇāv ṛtād adhy ādadāthe anṛtaṁ svena manyunā dakṣasya svena manyunā | yuvor itthādhi sadmasv apaśyāma hiraṇyayam | dhībhiś cana manasā svebhir akṣabhiḥ somasya svebhir akṣabhiḥ ||
english: When you two, O Mitra and Varuṇa, by your own will took hold of untruth beyond ṛta, by your own impulse of wisdom — in your very abodes we have seen the golden one. We have seen it with our thoughts, with our minds, with our own eyes, with the eyes of Soma's own.

sanskrit: yuvāṁ stomebhir devayanto aśvināśrāvayanta iva ślokam āyavo yuvāṁ havyābhy āyavaḥ | yuvor viśvā adhi śriyaḥ pṛkṣaś ca viśvavedasā | pruṣāyante vām pavayo hiraṇyaye rathe dasrā hiraṇyaye ||
english: The god-seeking descendants of Āyu have made their call resound to you Aśvins with their hymns, like a resonant sound; they called you two with their oblations. Upon you two who know all wealth, all glories and refreshments rest. The fellies of your golden chariot, O Dasras, sprinkle abundantly — of your golden chariot.

sanskrit: aceti dasrā vy u nākam ṛṇvatho yuñjate vāṁ rathayujo diviṣṭiṣv adhvasmāno diviṣṭiṣu | adhi vāṁ sthāma vandhure rathe dasrā hiraṇyaye | patheva yantāv anuśāsatā rajo añjasā śāsatā rajaḥ ||
english: It has become manifest, O Dasras — you two have opened up the vault of heaven; the chariot-yokers harness your car in the heavenly courses, without blemish in the heavenly courses. Your standing place is on the chariot-seat, O Dasras, on the golden chariot. Driving as if along a path, you guide the aerial space, swiftly guiding space.

sanskrit: śacībhir naḥ śacīvasū divā naktaṁ daśasyatam | mā vāṁ rātir upa dasat kadā canāsmad rātiḥ kadā cana ||
english: O Aśvins, rich in might, with your mighty deeds show favor to us by day and by night. May your bounty never fail us, never at any time may your gift to us fail.

sanskrit: vṛṣann indra vṛṣapāṇāsa indava ime sutā adriṣutāsa udbhidas tubhyaṁ sutāsa udbhidaḥ | te tvā mandantu dāvane mahe citrāya rādhase | gīrbhir girvāhaḥ stavamāna ā gahi sumṛḻīko na ā gahi ||
english: O mighty Indra, these are the inebriating Soma drops pressed by the stones, gushing forth, pressed out for you, gushing up. May they exhilarate you to give the great, the splendid bounty. O praised one, borne by hymns, come, lauded by songs; come to us as one most gracious.

sanskrit: o ṣū ṇo agne śṛṇuhi tvam īḻito devebhyo bravasi yajñiyebhyo rājabhyo yajñiyebhyaḥ | yad dha tyām aṅgirobhyo dhenum devā adadattana | vi tāṁ duhre aryamā kartarī sacāṁś eṣa tāṁ veda me sacā ||
english: O Agni, when invoked, do listen to us; you speak to the worshipful gods, the worthy kings to be worshipped. When once the gods bestowed that cow upon the Aṅgirases, Aryaman and the she-cutter milked her in company — that one I know in my own company.

sanskrit: mo ṣu vo asmad abhi tāni pauṁsyā sanā bhūvan dyumnāni mota jāriṣur asmat purota jāriṣuḥ | yad vaś citraṁ yuge-yuge navyaṁ ghoṣād amartyam | asmāsu tan maruto yac ca duṣṭaraṁ didhṛtā yac ca duṣṭaram ||
english: Let not those manly powers, those ancient glories of yours, fall away from us; let them not vanish from before us. Whatever of yours is wondrous, age after age renewed, resounding, immortal — that, O Maruts, fix upon us; and what is hard to win, fix that hard-won thing upon us.

sanskrit: dadhyaṅ ha me januṣam pūrvo aṅgirāḥ priyamedhaḥ kaṇvo atrir manuś vidus te me pūrve manur viduḥ | teṣāṁ deveṣv āyatir asmākaṁ teṣu nābhayaḥ | teṣāṁ padena mahy ā name gira indrāgnī ā name girā ||
english: Dadhyac, Aṅgiras the elder, Priyamedha, Kaṇva, Atri, and Manu — these knew my birth; those foremost ones, Manu knew. Their access is to the gods; our kinship lies with them. By their footstep may I bow down to the great one with my hymns — to Indra and Agni may I bow with my hymn.

sanskrit: hotā yakṣad vanino vanta vāryam bṛhaspatiṛ yajati veṇa ukṣabhiḥ puruvārebhir ukṣabhiḥ | jagṛbhmā dūrāādiśaṁ ślokam adrer adha tmanā | adhārayad ararindāni sukratuḥ purū sadmāni sukratuḥ ||
english: The Hotā priest shall worship, the trees of the forest shall receive the desired gift; Bṛhaspati sacrifices, and Veṇa with the bulls, with many-desired bulls. We have grasped the far-resounding call of the stone by its own power. The wise one of good purpose has upheld the yielding places — many abodes, the skilled one.

sanskrit: ye devāso divy ekādaśa stha pṛthivyām adhy ekādaśa stha | apsuṣito mahinaikādaśa stha te devāso yajñam imaṁ juṣadhvam ||
english: Ye gods who are eleven in heaven, who are eleven upon the earth, who dwell in the waters — ye eleven in your greatness — be pleased with this sacrifice of ours.

sanskrit: vediṣade priyadhāmāya sudyute dhāsim iva pra bharā yonim agnaye | vastreṇeva vāsayā manmanā śuciṁ jyotīrathaṁ śukravarṇaṁ tamohanaṁ ||
english: Bring the nourishment as if to its resting-place, to Agni who loves the sacred seat, who loves his dear abode, who blazes bright. Clothe him in your thought as with a garment — the pure one, the chariot of light, the bright-hued, the dispeller of darkness.

sanskrit: abhi dvijanmā trivṛd annam ṛjyate saṁvatsare vāvṛdhe jagdham ī punaḥ | anyasyāsā jihvayā jenyo vṛṣā ny anyena vanino mṛṣṭa vāraṇaḥ ||
english: Agni of double birth, with three-fold food, is urged on; he has grown throughout the year, eating and again consuming. With one mouth's tongue he is a hero worthy of song; with another he licks clean the trees, the defender.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇaprutau vevije asya sakṣitā ubhā tarete abhi mātarā śiśum | prācājihvaṁ dhvasayantaṁ tṛṣucyutam ā sācyaṁ kupayaṁ vardhanam pituḥ ||
english: His two abiding companions, the black and the tawny, tremble; both mothers bend over the child. Eastward-tongued, sending smoke aloft, poured from the ladle, bearing the companion of Kupa, the sustainer of his father.

sanskrit: mumukṣvo manaṁve mānavasya̱te raghudruvaḥ kṛṣṇasītāsa ū juvaḥ | asamanā ajirāso raghuṣyado vātajūtā upa yujyanta āśavaḥ ||
english: Eager to be freed, for Manu, for the offspring of Manu, the swift-rushing ones with black wake, the fleet ones — unequal, nimble, swift of leap, driven by the wind, the swift ones are yoked together.

sanskrit: ād asya te dhvasayanto vṛtherate kṛṣṇam abhvam mahi varpaḥ karikriataḥ | yat sīm mahīm avanim prābhi marmṛśad abhiśvasan stanayann eti nānadat ||
english: Then his attendants, scattering sparks, roam about; making a great form, a black, formidable one, crackling. When he eagerly licks across the broad earth, hissing, thundering, he goes roaring.

sanskrit: bhūṣan na yo 'dhi babhrūṣu namante vṛṣeva patnīr abhy eti roruvat | ojāyamānas tanvaś ca śumbhate bhīmo na śṛṅgā davidhāva durgṛbhiḥ ||
english: Like one who adorns himself, they bow above the tawny ones; like a bull approaching his mates, he comes bellowing. Growing in strength he makes his body resplendent; terrible as one wielding horns, he flourishes hard to grasp.

sanskrit: sa saṁstiro viṣṭiraḥ saṁ gṛbhāyati jānann eva jānatīr nitya ā śaye | punar vardhante api yanti devyam anyad varpaḥ pitroḥ kṛṇvate sacā ||
english: He who is spread out and spread abroad gathers himself; knowing, he lies ever among those who know. Again they grow and attain the divine; they take on another form together from both parents.

sanskrit: tam agruvaḥ keśinīḥ saṁ hi rebhira ūrdhvās tasthur mamruṣīḥ prāyave punaḥ | tāsāṁ jarām pramuñcann eti nānadad asu̱m paraṁ janayañ jīvam astṛtam ||
english: The long-haired, virgin ones have sung together to him; they stand erect, though seemingly dead, ready to go forth again. Loosening their age, he goes roaring, generating a supreme life, the un-felled living flame.

sanskrit: adhīvāsam pari mātū rihann aha tuvigrebhiḥ satvabhir yāti vi jrayaḥ | vayo dadhat padvate rerihat sadā nu śyenī sacate vartanīr aha ||
english: Licking round the garment of his mother, he goes forth with his great-eating heroes, spreading everywhere. Bestowing sustenance, he licks for the four-footed ever; the hawk-like one follows the paths of day.

sanskrit: asmāakam agne maghavasu dīdidhy adha śvasīvān vṛṣabho damūnāḥ | avāsyā śiśumatīr adīder varmeiva yutsu parijarbhurāṇaḥ ||
english: Shine forth, O Agni, among our patrons; then like a roaring bull, the household lord. You have shone upon the mothers with their young who are to be unveiled — like armor in battle, thundering around them.

sanskrit: idam agne sudhitaṁ durdhitād adhi priyād u cin manmanaḥ preyo astu te | yat te śukraṁ tanvo rocate śuci tenāsmabhyaṁ vanase ratnam ā tvam ||
english: O Agni, may this that is well-uttered be more dear to you than what is ill-uttered, even than what is cherished in the heart; may it be more pleasing to you. By that bright, pure glory that blazes from your body, do win for us a treasure.

sanskrit: rathāya nāvam uta no gṛhāya nityāritrām padvatīṁ rāsy agne | asmākaṁ vīrāṁ uta no maghono janāṁś ca yā pārayāc charma yā ca ||
english: O Agni, grant us a boat for the chariot, for our house a vessel with a perpetual rudder, bearing feet. And may it carry across our heroes, our bountiful ones, and our people — carrying them safely across.

sanskrit: abhī no agna uktham ij juguryā dyāvākṣāmā sindhavas ca svagūrtāḥ | gavyaṁ yavyaṁ yanto dīrghāheṣaṁ varam aruṇyo varanta ||
english: O Agni, may heaven, earth, and the waters, well-pleased, guard our utterance. Going forward seeking cattle and grain, with long call may the reddish ones claim the boon.

sanskrit: baḷ itthā tad vapuṣe dhāyi darśataṁ devasya bhargaḥ sahaso yato jani | yad īm upa hvarate sādhate matir ṛtasya dhenā anayanta sasrutaḥ ||
english: Truly so — for beauty it was fashioned, the visible splendor of the god born of power. When the inspired thought draws near and accomplishes its purpose, the streams of ṛta flow on and are led forth.

sanskrit: pṛkṣo vapuḥ pitumān nitya ā śaye dvitīyam ā saptaśivāsu mātṛṣu | tṛtīyam asya vṛṣabhasya dohase daśapramatiṁ janayanta yoṣaṇaḥ ||
english: His nourishing form, full of food, lies ever in his place; a second is among the seven kindly mothers. A third of this bull is for milking — the ten-directing one — the women bring it forth.

sanskrit: nir yad īm budhnān mahiṣasya varpaṣa īśānāsaḥ śavasā kranta sūrayaḥ | yad īm anu pradivo madhva ādhave guhā santaṁ mātariśvā mathāyati ||
english: When the wise, sovereign ones with power step forth from the base of the mighty bull's form — when following from the primeval time, from the sweetness of the pressing, Mātariśvan churns what is hidden within.

sanskrit: pra yat pituḥ paramān nīyate pary ā pṛkṣudho vīrudho daṁsu rohati | ubhā yad asya januṣaṁ yad invata ād id yaviṣṭho abhavad ghṛṇā śuciḥ ||
english: When he is led forth from the highest of his fathers, round about plants and creeping things grow thick and lush. When both mothers set in motion his birth — then the youngest one blazed up, pure with radiant glow.

sanskrit: ād in mātṝr āviśad yāsv ā śucir ahiṁsyamāna urviyā vi vāvṛdhe | anu yat pūrvā aruhat sanājuvo ni navyaṣīṣv avarasā dhāvate ||
english: Then he entered his mothers in whom he shines pure; unhurt, he grew abundantly. Climbing his former timeless ones who were ever-swift, he glides downward into newer and lower ones.

sanskrit: ād id dhotāraṁ vṛṇate diviṣṭiṣu bhagam iva papṛcānāsa ṛñjate | devān yat kratvā majmanā puruṣṭuto martaṁ śaṁsaṁ viśvadhā veti dhāyase ||
english: Then they choose him as the Hotā at the heavenly journeys; they go to meet him as if anointing Bhaga. When, wide-praised in wisdom and greatness, he goes altogether seeking mortal praise to sustain himself.

sanskrit: vi yad asthād yajato vātacodito hvāro na vakvā jaraṇā anākṛtaḥ | tasya patman dakṣuṣaḥ kṛṣṇajaṁhasaḥ śucijanmano raja ā vyadhvanaḥ ||
english: When the worshipful one driven by wind stands forth — crooked as a snake, advancing with age but not weakened — on the path of that eager one of dark strides and pure birth, the realm of space was shot through.

sanskrit: ratho na yātaḥ śikvabhiḥ kṛto dyām aṅgebhir aruṣebhir īyate | ād asya te kṛṣṇāso dakṣi sūrayaḥ śūrasyeva tveṣathād īṣate vayaḥ ||
english: Like a chariot driven by the skilled, built with skill, he moves through heaven with his red-glowing limbs. Then his dark, keen ones, the wise patrons — like the swiftness of a hero — they take wing with impetuosity.

sanskrit: tvayā hy agne varuṇo dhṛtavrato mitraḥ śāśadre aryamā sudānavaḥ | yat sīm anu kratuṇā viśvathā vibhur arān na nemiḥ paribhūr ajāyathāḥ ||
english: Through you, O Agni, Varuṇa of firm ordinance, and Mitra, and Aryaman of good gifts have been established. Following their purpose, all-pervading everywhere, you were born as one who encompasses all, as the felloe encompasses the spokes.

sanskrit: tvam agne śaśamānāya sunvate ratnaṁ yaviṣṭha devatātim invasi | taṁ tvā nu navyaṁ sahaso yuvan vayam bhagaṁ na kāre mahiratna dhīmahi ||
english: You, O Agni, youngest, send the divine bounty to the striving one who presses Soma. You, ever new, scion of strength — let us now focus upon you as upon Bhaga in our work, O bearer of great treasure.

sanskrit: asme rayiṁ na svarthaṁ damūnasam bhagaṁ dakṣaṁ na papṛcāsi dharṇasim | raśmīm̐r iva yo yamati janmanī ubhe devānāṁ śaṁsam ṛta ā ca sukratuḥ ||
english: You have not blended upon us the household wealth like the Sun's bounty, the portion and power supporting us. He who guides both births like reins — of the gods' praise and of ṛta — he is the wise one of good purpose.

sanskrit: uta na sudyotmā jīrāśvo hotā mandraḥ śṛṇavac candrarathaḥ | sa no neṣan neṣatamairu amūro agnir vāmaṁ suvitaṁ vasyo accha ||
english: And may the brightly shining, swift-horsed, joyful Hotā, with his gleaming chariot, hear us. May Agni, the blameless one with the finest charioteers, lead us — lead us toward the good, toward well-being, toward wealth.

sanskrit: astāvy agniḥ śimīvadbhir arkaiḥ sāmrājyāya prataraṁ dadhānaḥ | amī ca ye maghavāno vayaṁ ca mihaṁ na sūro ati niṣ ṭatanyuḥ ||
english: Agni has been praised with energetic hymns, laying the groundwork for universal sovereignty. Both those bounteous ones and we ourselves — like the sun through mist, we have burst forth in brightness.

sanskrit: samiddho agna ā vaha devāṁ adya yatasruce | tantuṁ tanuṣva pūrvyaṁ sutasomāya dāśuṣe ||
english: O Agni, enkindled, bring the gods hither today for the one who reaches out with the ladle. Extend the primeval thread for the generous one who has pressed the Soma.

sanskrit: ghṛtavantam upa māsi madhumantaṁ tanūnapāt | yajñaṁ viprasya māvataḥ śaśamānasya dāśuṣaḥ ||
english: O Tanūnapāt, thou dost approach the ghee-filled, honey-sweet sacrifice of this inspired, well-disposed, and generous worshipper.

sanskrit: śuciḥ pāvako adbhuto madhvā yajñam mimikṣati | narāśaṁsas trir ā divo devo deveṣu yajñiyaḥ ||
english: Pure and purifying, wonderful, Narāśaṁsa sprinkles the sacrifice with sweetness. The god, worthy of worship among gods, comes down three times from heaven.

sanskrit: īḻito agna ā vaha indraṁ citram iha priyam | iyaṁ hi tvā matir mamā acchā sujihva vacyate ||
english: O Agni, invoked, bring here the dear and wondrous Indra. For this thought of mine calls to you, O fair-tongued one.

sanskrit: stṛṇānāso yatasruco barhir yajñe svadhvare | vṛñje devavyacastamam indrāya śarma saprathaḥ ||
english: Spreading the litter, reaching out with the ladle at the sacrifice, at the well-ordered rite, I choose the most god-reaching, wide-spreading shelter for Indra.

sanskrit: vi śrayantām ṛtāvṛdhaḥ prayai devebhyo mahīḥ | pāvakāsaḥ puruspṛho dvāro devīr asaścataḥ ||
english: Let the great divine doors, upholders of ṛta, swing open for the passing of the gods, the purifying, much-desired, never-failing divine doors.

sanskrit: ā bhandamāne upāke naktoṣāsā supeśasā | yahvī ṛtasya mātarā sīdatām barhir ā sumat ||
english: The two rejoicing, close at hand, fair-formed Night and Dawn — the two great mothers of ṛta — may they take their seat on the sacred grass, bringing good things.

sanskrit: mandrajihvā jugurvaṇī hotārā daivyā kavī | yajñaṁ no yakṣatām imaṁ sidhram adya divispṛśam ||
english: The two divine seers, the Hotā-priests with honey-tongued voices, ever welcoming — may the two poets sacrifice this our offering today, bringing it surely to the sky-touching goal.

sanskrit: śucir deveṣv arpitā hotrā marutsu bhāratī | iḻā sarasvatī mahī barhiḥ sīdantu yajñiyāḥ ||
english: Pure Hotrā, laid before the gods among the Maruts, is Bhāratī. Iḷā, Sarasvatī, and Mahī — the three goddesses worthy of worship — let them sit on the sacrificial grass.

sanskrit: tan nas turīpam adbhutam puru vāram puru tmanā | tvaṣṭā poṣāya vi ṣyatu rāye nābhā no asmayuḥ ||
english: May Tvaṣṭar, who loves us, the center of riches, release that wonderful nourishment, full of many gifts, bountiful by his very nature, for prosperity and wealth.

sanskrit: avasṛjann upa tmanā devān yakṣi vanaspate | agnir havyā suṣūdati devo deveṣu medhiraḥ ||
english: O Vanaspati, send forth and worship the gods of your own accord. Agni, the wise god among gods, will convey the oblations rightly.

sanskrit: pūṣaṇvate marutvate viśvadevāya vāyave | svāhā gāyatravepase havyam indrāya kartana ||
english: To Pūṣan's company, to the Marut-host, to the All-Gods, to Vāyu — svāhā! Make the oblation to Indra who is moved by the Gāyatrī.

sanskrit: svāhākṛtāny ā gahy upa havyāni vītaye | indrā gahi śrudhī havaṁ tvāṁ havante adhvare ||
english: Come here to the things consecrated with svāhā; come to the oblations for your pleasure. Come here, O Indra, hear the call — they call you at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: pra tavyasīṁ navyasīṁ dhītim agnaye vāco matiṁ sahasaḥ sūnave bhare | apāṁ napād yo vasubhiḥ saha priyo hotā pṛthivyāṁ ny asīdad ṛtviyaḥ ||
english: I bring a stronger and newer thought, an utterance of speech, to Agni, son of strength. He, the child of the waters, who dwells dear with the Vasus, the Hotā, has taken his seat on the earth in due season.

sanskrit: sa jāyamānaḥ parame vyomany āvir agnir abhavan mātariśvane | asya kratvā samidhānasya majmanā pra dyāvā śociḥ pṛthivī arocayat ||
english: Being born in the highest heaven, Agni became manifest to Mātariśvan. By the wisdom of this enkindled one, by his greatness, he made heaven and earth shine brilliantly with his radiance.

sanskrit: asya tveṣā ajarā asya bhānavaḥ susaṁdṛśaḥ supratīkasya sudyutaḥ | bhātvakṣaso aty aktur na sindhavo 'gne rejante asanto ajarāḥ ||
english: His fierce, ageless rays, the rays of this fair-faced, brightly blazing one are beautiful to behold. Like rivers flowing past the night, blazing and ageless, O Agni, they flash.

sanskrit: yam erire bhṛgavo viśvavedosaṁ nābhā pṛthivyā bhuvanasya majmanā | agniṁ taṁ gīrbhir hinuhi sva ā dame ya eko vasvo varuṇo na rājati ||
english: Him whom the Bhṛgus set in motion, all-knowing, at the navel of the earth, at the center of existence — urge that Agni with your hymns in your own home, he who alone rules over riches as Varuṇa rules.

sanskrit: na yo varāya marutām iva svanaḥ seneva sṛṣṭā divyā yathāśaniḥ | agnir jambhais tigitair atti bharvati yo̱dho na śatrūn sa vanā ny ṛñjate ||
english: None can prevent him, like the roar of the Maruts; like a hurled army, like the bolt of heaven — Agni devours and consumes with his sharp teeth; like a warrior driving back his foes, he overpowers the forests.

sanskrit: kuvin no agnir ucathasya vīr asad vasuṣ kuvid vasubhiḥ kāmam āvarat | codaḥ kuvit tutujyāt sātaye dhiyaḥ śucipratīkaṁ tam ayā dhiyā gṛṇe ||
english: Will Agni be a hero worthy of our praise? Will the good one bring wealth and desires with his riches? Will the impeller speed our prayers to the winning? With this thought I praise him of bright face.

sanskrit: ghṛtapratīkaṁ va ṛtasya dhūrṣadam agnim mitraṁ na samidhāna ṛñjate | indhāno akro vidatheṣu dīdyac chukravarṇām ud u no yaṁsate dhiyam ||
english: The one with ghee-bright face, seated in the pole of ṛta — enkindled, men approach Agni as they approach Mitra. The enkindled, active one blazing at assemblies — may he raise up our bright-hued thought.

sanskrit: aprayuccann aprayucchadbhir agne śivebhiḥ naḥ pāyubhiḥ pāhi śagmaiḥ | adabdhebhir adṛpitebhir iṣṭe 'nimiṣadbhiḥ pari pāhi no jāḥ ||
english: O Agni, never faltering, with your unfaltering, gracious, effective guardians protect us. With your unerring, undeceived, unswerving, unwinking guards, protect our offspring all around.

sanskrit: eti pra hotā vratam asya māyayor dhvāṁ dadhānaḥ śucipeśasaṁ dhiyam | abhi srucaḥ kramate dakṣiṇāvṛto yā asya dhāma prathamaṁ ha niṁsate ||
english: The Hotā goes forward, carrying out the ordinance of these two enchanters, holding aloft the pure-formed thought. He strides toward the ladles, turning to the right — those that have from the beginning licked his station.

sanskrit: abhīm ṛtasya dohanā anūṣata yonau devasya sadane parīvṛtāḥ | apām upasthe vibhṛto yad āvasad adha svadhā adhayad yābhir īyate ||
english: The milch-vessels of ṛta have sung along for him, in the divine abode, in the womb, enclosed around. When, nourished in the lap of the waters, he dwelt there — then the self-ordering one drank from those by which he moves.

sanskrit: yuyūṣataḥ savayasā tad id vapuḥ samānam arthaṁ vitarītratā mithaḥ | ād īm bhago na havyaḥ sam asmad ā voḻhur na raśmīn sam ayaṁsta sārathiḥ ||
english: The two of equal age, wishing to separate, share indeed that one form with a common purpose, yet excel each other mutually. Then, like Bhaga who is to be invoked, as a charioteer gathers the reins, he gathered himself together from us.

sanskrit: yam īṁ dvā savayasā saparyataḥ samāne yonā mithunā samokanā | divā na naktam palito yuvājani purū carann ajaro mānuṣā yugā ||
english: Him whom two equals together worship, dwelling in the same womb, a pair sharing one abode — neither by day nor by night does his grey old age befall him; moving through many human ages, he is ageless.

sanskrit: tam īṁ hinvanti dhītayo daśa vriśo devam martāsa ūtaye havāmahe | dhanor adhi pravata ā sa ṛṇvaty abhivrajadbhir vayunā navādhita ||
english: Ten sisters urge him forward; mortals call upon this god for help. From a slope of the bow he rushes with those who come clustering, assigned to new tracks.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hy agne divyasya rājasi tvaṁ pārthivasya paśupā iva tmanā | enī ta ete bṛhatī abhiśriyā hiraṇyayī vakvarī barhir āśāte ||
english: You, O Agni, reign over the heavenly realm; you are like the guardian of cattle for the earthly realm by your own nature. These two great tawny ones, radiant with glory, golden and graceful, lie down upon the sacred grass for you.

sanskrit: agne juṣasva prati harya tad vaco mandra svadhāva ṛtajāta sukrato | yo viśvataḥ pratyaṅṅ asi darśato raṇvaḥ saṁdṛṣṭau pitumām̐ iva kṣayaḥ ||
english: O Agni, receive and love that speech, O joyful, self-nourishing, born of ṛta, wise one. You who face outward in all directions, visible, pleasant to behold, like a nourishing abode when seen.

sanskrit: tam pṛcchatā sa jagāmā sa veda sa cikitvāṁ īyate sā nv īyate | tasmin santi praśiṣas tasmin iṣṭayaḥ sa vājasya śavasaḥ śuṣmiṇas patiḥ ||
english: Ask of him — he has gone, he knows; the discerning one moves, now he moves indeed. In him are the teachings, in him are the offerings; he is the lord of vigor, of strength, of power.

sanskrit: tam it pṛcchanti na simo vi pṛcchati sveneva dhīro manasā yad agrabhīt | na mṛṣyate prathamaṁ nāparaṁ vaco 'sya kratvā sacate apradṛpitaḥ ||
english: They ask of him; but he does not divide to ask — when the wise one grasps it as with his own mind. He does not misapprehend the first word, nor the latter; by his wisdom one attends on him, undespised.

sanskrit: tam id gacchanti juhvas tam arvatīr viśvāny ekaḥ śṛṇavad vacāṁsi me | purupraīṣas taturir yajñasādhano 'cchidrottiḥ śiśur ādatta saṁ rabhaḥ ||
english: To him go the ladles, to him go the oblation-bearers; may he alone hear all my words. With many impulses, swift, accomplishing sacrifice, the young one of unbroken help takes hold and grasps eagerly.

sanskrit: upasthāyaṁ carati yat samārata sadyo jātas tat sāra yujyebhiḥ | abhi śvāntam mṛśate nāndye mude yad īṁ gacchanty uśatīr apiṣṭhitam ||
english: Coming near, he moves about, all ready; newborn, he goes at once with his companions to the goal. He touches the gladdened one with joy, for delight, when the eager ones approach him as he rests upon them.

sanskrit: sa īm mṛgo apyo vanargur upa tvacy upamasyāṁ ni dhāyi | vy abravīd vayunā martyebhyo 'gnir vidvāṁ ṛtacid dhi satyaḥ ||
english: That wild beast, of the waters, the forest-rover, has been set down close beside the topmost skin. Agni, knowing, truly finding ṛta, declared the paths to mortals — for he is indeed true.

sanskrit: trimūrdhānaṁ saptaraśmiṁ gṛṇīṣe 'nūnam agnim pitror upasthe | niṣattam asya carato dhruvasya viśvā divo rocanā apprivāṁsam ||
english: I praise Agni of three heads and seven rays, undiminished, in the lap of his two parents. Seated, of one who moves yet is fixed, he has filled all the luminous realms of heaven.

sanskrit: ukṣā mahām̐ abhi vavakṣa ene ajaras tasthāv itaūtir ṛṣvaḥ | urvyāḥ pado ni dadhāti sānau rihany ūdho aruṣāso asya ||
english: The great bull has spread himself over these two, the ageless one stands mighty, with aid from the hither side. He sets the foot of the broad one on the summit; his red-glowing ones lick his udder.

sanskrit: samānaṁ vatsam abhi saṁcarantī viṣvag dhenū vi carataḥ sumeke | anaparjyāṁ adhvano mimāne viśvān ketāṁ adhi maho dadhāne ||
english: Moving about together toward their common calf, the two well-built cows wander in different directions. Measuring out the paths without deviation, receiving all purposes upon the great one.

sanskrit: dhīrāsaḥ padaṁ kavayo nayanti nānā hṛdā rakṣamāṇā ajuryam | siṣāsantaḥ pary apaśyanta sindhum āvir ebhyo abhavat sūryo nṛṇ ||
english: The wise seers lead to the station, guarding the indestructible one with varying hearts. Desiring to win, they looked around upon the stream; the sun became manifest to these men.

sanskrit: didṛkṣeṇyaḥ pari kāṣṭhāsu jenya īḻenyo maho arbhāya jīvase | purutrā yad abhavat sūr ahaibhyo garbhebhyo maghavā viśvadarśataḥ ||
english: Visible in all quarters, worthy of hymning, praiseworthy, worthy of praise for great and small alike to live. When the sun arose for those of this day, the bountiful one became visible to all the embryos of the world.

sanskrit: kathā te agne śucayanta āyor dadāśur vājebhir āśuṣāṇāḥ | ubhe yat toke tanaye dadhānā ṛtasya sāman raṇayanta devāḥ ||
english: How, O Agni, did the purifying ones of Āyu bestow their gifts on you, gaining swiftly with their prizes? When the gods, holding both offspring and progeny, made merry at the song of ṛta.

sanskrit: bodhā me asya vacaso yaviṣṭha maṁhiṣṭhasya prabhṛtasya svadhāvaḥ | pīyati tvo anu tvo gṛṇāti vandārus te tanvaṁ vande agne ||
english: Hear this my word, O youngest, O self-nourishing, bountiful bearer of the most generous offering. One reviles you, another praises you in turn; I, a worshipper, worship your body, O Agni.

sanskrit: ye pāyavo māmateyaṁ te agne paśyanto andhaṁ duritād arakṣan | rarakṣa tān sukṛto viśvavedā dipsanta id ripavo nāha debhuḥ ||
english: Those watchmen, O Agni, children of Māmateya, seeing the blind, protected him from wrongdoing. The all-knowing one who does good deeds has protected them; the foes who sought to harm them have not deceived them at all.

sanskrit: yo no agne aravivāṁ aghāyur arātivā marcayati dvayena | mantro guruḥ punar astu so asmā anu mṛkṣīṣṭa tanvaṁ duru̱ktaiḥ ||
english: The enemy of ours, O Agni, the malevolent one, the niggard who would harm us with his deceit — may the weighty spell recoil upon him; may his body be smeared with ill words.

sanskrit: uta vā yaḥ sahasya pravivdān marto martaṁ marcayati dvayena | ataḥ pāhi stavamāna stuvantam agne mākir no duritāya dhāyīḥ ||
english: Or if some powerful mortal, knowing evil, harms another mortal with deceit — from that protect the one who praises you, who lauds you, O Agni; let nothing lead us toward wrongdoing.

sanskrit: mathīd yad īṁ viṣṭo mātariśvā hotāraṁ viśvāpsuṁ viśvadevyam | ni yaṁ dadhur manuṣyāsu vikṣu svar ṇa citraṁ vapuṣe vibhāvam ||
english: When the pervading Mātariśvan churned forth the Hotā, rich in all forms, belonging to all gods — him whom they placed among the human tribes, shining with a wondrous, brilliant form like the sun.

sanskrit: dadānam in na dadabhanta manmāgnir varūtham mama tasya cākan | juṣanta viśvāny asya karmopastutim bharamāṇasya kāroḥ ||
english: Those who give — the thought does not harm them — Agni has chosen to be my shelter. May they delight in all his deeds, in the praise of the bard who bears the offering.

sanskrit: nitye cin nu yaṁ sadane jagṛbhre praśastibhir dadhire yajñiyāsaḥ | pra sū nayanta gṛbhayanta iṣṭāv aśvāso na rathyo rārahāṇāḥ ||
english: Him whom the worthy worshippers have grasped even in his own abode and established with praises — leading him forward, seizing him at the offering, like racing chariot-horses neighing in delight.

sanskrit: purūṇi dasmo ni riṇāti jambhair ād rocate vana ā vibhāvā | ād asya vāto anu vāti śocir astur na śaryām asanām anu dyūn ||
english: The wondrous one breaks down many things with his jaws; then he gleams, the all-brilliant one, in the forest. Then the wind blows behind his flame; like an archer shooting arrows, he sends it through the days.

sanskrit: na yaṁ ripavo na riṣaṇyavo garbhe santaṁ reṣaṇā reṣayanti | andhā apaśyā na dabhan abhikhyā nityāsa īm pretāro arakṣan ||
english: The foes, the harming ones, do not injure him while he abides in the womb; the blind, unseeing ones cannot harm him by their glance. His own eternal guardians protect him as he goes forth.

sanskrit: mahaḥ sa rāya eṣate patir dann ina inasya vasunaś pada ā | upa dhrajantam adrayo vidhann it ||
english: The master goes seeking great wealth; he who gives, the powerful lord of the powerful — of riches, at the station — the stones serve only him who presses on.

sanskrit: sa yo vṛṣā narāṁ na rodasyor śravobhir asti jīvapītasargaḥ | pra yaḥ sasrāṇaḥ śiśrīta yonau ||
english: He who is the bull, not of men, not of the two worlds — he who exists in fame, pouring forth a life-giving stream — who flows forward and clings to his birthplace.

sanskrit: ā yaḥ puraṁ nārmiṇīm adīded atyaḥ kavir nabhanyo nārvā | sūro na rukkvāñ chatātmā ||
english: He who has shone upon the unassailed stronghold — the swift, wise one, the cloud-born, not to be warded off — blazing like the sun, of hundredfold nature.

sanskrit: abhi dvijanmā trī rocanāni viśvā rajāṁsi śuśucāno asthāt | hotā yajiṣṭho apāṁ sadhasthe ||
english: Agni of double birth, blazing, has stood over the three luminous realms, over all the spaces. He is the most effective Hotā, in the abode of the waters.

sanskrit: ayaṁ sa hotā yo dvijanmā viśvā dadhev vāryāṇi śrasyaḥ | marto yo asmai sutuko dadāśa ||
english: He it is, the Hotā, he of double birth, who bears all desirable things, worthy of praise. Happy is the mortal who generously gives to him.

sanskrit: puru tvā dāśvān voce 'rir agne tava svid ā | todasye̍va śaraṇa ā mahasya ||
english: O Agni, I the bountiful one would call you a stranger, a near kinsman. Like shelter in the greatness of one who goads.

sanskrit: vy aninasya dhaninaḥ prahoṣe cid araruṣaḥ | kadā cana prajigato adevayoḥ ||
english: Of the unniggardly, wealthy one — even among those going vigorously forward — even of those not honoring the gods — when at any time they depart.

sanskrit: sa candro vipra martyo maho vrādhantamo divi | pra-pret te agne vanuṣaḥ syāma ||
english: He, the bright one, the inspired mortal of the great ones, most exuberant in heaven — may we, O Agni, be among the winners of your favor.
